one_liner: WooCommerce is a free, open-source WordPress plugin whose REST API (wc/v3) is authenticated with merchant-generated consumer key/secret, so a builder can self-host a store and test right away.
auth_notes: Merchant generates a Consumer Key/Secret in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. The key is the Basic Auth username and the secret is the password. OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA1 signing over HTTP is the reason OTHER is listed (from a third-party page, not re-verified here). WordPress Application Passwords are used for the MCP Adapter path. There is no OAuth2 flow for the core REST API.
access_notes: No developer programme or application is needed. WooCommerce is a free plugin, so a developer can run a store on their own WordPress site and generate keys. Each customer's store is self-hosted, so a store URL has to be collected per user.
blocker_notes: Each user must supply their own store URL and generate keys. HTTPS is recommended and pretty permalinks are required. These are per-customer setup steps, not blockers for the builder.
